title: Equivalence arrows are initial in the fixed-source twisted-arrow simplicial set
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges, initial objects and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the ordered join from [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory and $x\in\mathcal C_0$. For $n\geq0$, let $(P_x)_n$ consist of maps $N([n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n])\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction to the first ordered block is the constant map at $x$. The operator for $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ is precomposition with $N(\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta)$. Assume that the resulting simplicial set $P_x$ is a quasicategory. Every equivalence edge $f:x\to y$ of $\mathcal C$, viewed as a vertex of $P_x$, is initial: for every vertex $g$ of $P_x$, $\operatorname{Map}_{P_x}(f,g)$ is weakly contractible. In particular the degenerate identity edge at $x$ is initial in $P_x$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1: initiality of an equivalence arrow in the fixed-source twisted-arrow category. Only the initiality conclusion is used; the quasicategory property of P_x is assumed separately here to keep this auxiliary statement independent of its parent left-fibration theorem. Kerodon tag 03JW, not a Stacks tag. Online statement and full proof read; archival source WANTED.
